source: WHO Weekly Epidemiological Record, 'Cholera, 2005', WER 2006;81(31):297-307
processing_notes: Source confirms zero cholera transmission 2005-01-01..2005-12-31. Source states: 'No cases were reported from the Horn of Africa during 2005.'. Evidence type: Documented_Absence. Surveillance system status during absence: operational. AGENT 3 ZERO-TRANSMISSION VALIDATION. Calendar year 2005, national. TWO INDEPENDENT WHO STATEMENTS: (1) this WER annual cholera report states affirmatively that no cases were reported from the Horn of Africa during 2005; (2) the WHO Global Health Observatory annual cholera series carries an EXPLICIT zero for Ethiopia in 2005 (cases 0, deaths 0, CFR 0) - one of 20 countries recorded with a formal nil return that year, as against years that are simply absent from the series. A third, national source agrees: EPHI/IVI, Clin Infect Dis 2024;79(Suppl 1):S8 Table 1 gives Ethiopia 0 cases and 0 deaths for 2005. SURVEILLANCE STATUS: operational. Ethiopia reported to WHO continuously across 2004-2010 and reported SIXTEEN cases for 2004 (GHO; same WER series) - a system that notifies 16 cases in one year and a nil return the next is a system that was looking. REGIONAL CROSS-CHECK: a regionally QUIET period, so this is the easy case rather than the demanding one. GHO 2005 for the neighbours: Eritrea explicit 0, Kenya 816, and no 2005 entry at all for Djibouti, Somalia, Sudan or South Sudan. [AGENT 3 REVISION 2026-09-19] AWD-TERMINOLOGY STRESS TEST, APPLIED AFTER THIS ROW WAS WRITTEN AND PASSED. Ethiopia used 'acute watery diarrhoea' in place of 'cholera' before 2019, so a WHO cholera nil return can in principle hide an AWD epidemic - that is exactly why Agent 3 retracted its own 2011 zero row (former Index 397), after finding WHO/HSE/GAR/DCE/2011.3 reporting AWD in Afar, Somali and Oromia as of 15 July 2011. The 2005 row survives the same test for three reasons. (1) The terminology did NOT stop Ethiopia reporting in this era: Ethiopia returned 16 cholera cases for 2004 and 54,070 for 2006 to the same WHO collection, and WER 81(41):385-386 'Outbreak news: Acute watery diarrhoeal syndrome, Ethiopia' shows the Ethiopian Ministry of Health notifying WHO of 22,101 AWD cases and 219 deaths as of 28 September 2006 with V. cholerae O1 Inaba confirmed - i.e. Ethiopian AWD outbreaks WERE reaching WHO under the cholera heading in 2004-2010. The reporting relationship only lapsed after 2010. (2) A targeted search of the WHO IRIS corpus for Ethiopian AWD documents dated 2005 returned nothing, whereas the equivalent search for 2006 immediately returned the Outbreak News item above. (3) WER 'Cholera, 2006' dates the Ethiopian epidemic's onset to April 2006, when the South Sudan outbreak 'crossed to Gambella, Ethiopia, in April', which is consistent with a quiet 2005. (reason: Agent 3: AWD-terminology stress test applied to the 2005 zero row after the 2011 row failed the same test)

processing_notes: Source confirms zero cholera transmission 2011-12-12..2014-12-12. REGIONAL CONTEXT: within-Ethiopia quiet period (the 2015-17 national wave began in epi-week 35 of 2015; Tigray regional zero weeks 2015 W31/W39-41/W50-51 are Index 1008-1010) while Kenya and Somalia had active 2015 epidemics far to the south-east - absence here is local. However, the Region has experienced outbreaks of AWD in the years 2007 - 2009.'. Evidence type: Documented_Absence. Surveillance system status during absence: operational. AGENT 3 (opus55) batch 1 Q7. REGIONAL documented absence, deliberately SHORTENED and LOW-CONFIDENCE. The assessment (June 2013) claims three AWD-free years (i.e. from ~June 2010), but that start is CONTRADICTED: OCHA/EHNRI list Jile Timuga woreda (Amhara, Oromo Special Zone) among AWD-reporting woredas in the two weeks to 3 Oct 2010 (presence record, source 183), and a March 2011 FETP thesis says 'Amhara is one of the regions that have been affected by AWD, meningitis and measles outbreaks in the year 2009 and 2010' (source 201). The window therefore starts 1 Jan 2011 and ends 31 May 2013 (the assessment's data period). INDEPENDENT SUPPORT for 2011-2013: Zekarias Adamu (source 266, Index 1700-1709) AWD = 0 in 10 Amhara woredas Jul-Oct 2011 while 33,855 malaria cases were counted; Amhara hazard profiles in two 2015 FETP theses (Getachew Abebe 5c12eb26; Misganaw Ayalew 9bb513a0) list AWD outbreaks only for '2006-2009'; woreda zeros Jan-May 2013 in Awi/West Gojjam (Index 1805-1809) and North Wollo/Wag Himra (Index 2639-2643); no positive Amhara row or presence record anywhere in the file for 2011-2013. REGIONAL CROSS-CHECK - DEMANDING CASE: AWD was reported in neighbouring Afar, Oromia, Somali, Dire Dawa and Harari in 2011 (Index 715-720, presence 2011) and in Dibate woreda, Metekel (Benishangul-Gumuz, bordering Amhara's Awi zone) in Feb-Mar 2012 (Index 1929), so absence here needs a strong source and this one is a needs-assessment summary, not a surveillance table - hence confidence 0.5. Source states: 'Acute Watery Diarrhea Within the past three years no AWD was registered with in the health institutions of assessed woredas.'. Evidence type: Documented_Absence. Surveillance system status during absence: partial. AGENT 3 (opus55) batch 1 Q9. Woreda documented absence from the Afar Belg season health assessment of 2015 (assessed woredas Awra and Teru of Zone 4; Megale, Berahle, Bidu and Dalol of Zone 2) reproduced in an Ethiopian FETP thesis. DATING: 'within the past three years' counted back from the Jan-May 2015 data period = Jun 2012-May 2015. SURVEILLANCE: health-institution registers were reviewed; the same section counts 3,533 malaria cases Jan-May 2015 by woreda and month, reports no suspected measles and one suspected meningitis death in Barahle - but woreda PHEM capacity in Afar was weak, hence 'partial'. CAUTION: the identical sentence appears in a second thesis covering a different set of Afar woredas from the same regional assessment (Ibrahim Hussein, source 380) - a shared assessment-report template, not a copied result, but it lowers confidence. No positive Afar row or presence record exists for Jun 2012-May 2015 (Afar's two 2015 cases are Aug-Dec 2015, Index 444); OCHA's Nov 2014 Burimedayto alert was lab-negative (Index 1987). REGIONAL CONTEXT: national 2012-2014 undetermined; Somalia reported cholera every year 2012-2015. Provincial subset - do not sum with national row.

source: Ibrahim Hussein, Compiled Body of Works in Field Epidemiology, Ethiopian FETP, Addis Ababa University, May 2016 (AAU ETD) - Afar Belg season assessment May 2015, Zones 1, 3 and 5 (Elidaar, Kori, Chifra, Gewane, Amibara, Awash Fentale, Hadelela, Dalifage)
processing_notes: Source confirms zero cholera transmission 2012-06-01..2015-05-31. Source states: 'Acute Watery Diarrhea: Within the past three years no AWD was registered with in the health institutions of assessed wereda.'. Evidence type: Documented_Absence. Surveillance system status during absence: partial. AGENT 3 (opus55) batch 1 Q10. Woreda documented absence from the Afar Belg season assessment of May 2015 (8 assessed woredas of Zones 1, 3 and 5 holding 111 health institutions) reproduced in an Ethiopian FETP thesis. DATING: 'within the past three years' counted back from the Jan-May 2015 data period = Jun 2012-May 2015. SURVEILLANCE 'partial': the same chapter counts 21,769 confirmed malaria cases Jan-May 2015 by zone and month and 36 measles cases in Gewane, Awash Fentale and Dalifage, but its own Table 2.16 shows a functional PHEM unit in only 4 of the 8 woredas (Elidaar, Chifra, Amibara, Dalifage). CAUTION: the identical sentence appears in a second thesis on other Afar woredas of the same regional assessment (Endris Ali, source 379) - shared template; confidence lowered accordingly. No positive Afar row or presence record exists for Jun 2012-May 2015. Awash Fentale's window starts 2012-07-08 to abut, not overlap, its EFY-2004 zero (Index 1001). REGIONAL CONTEXT: Amibara/Gewane/Awash Fentale lie on the Awash corridor that carried the 2006-2009 Afar epidemics; national 2012-2014 undetermined. Provincial subset - do not sum with national row.

source: Woubayehu Kassa, Compiled Body of Works in Field Epidemiology, Ethiopian FETP, Addis Ababa University, November 2014 (AAU ETD) - Oromia Belg season assessment 2013, East and West Hararghe zones (data January-May 2013)
processing_notes: Source confirms zero cholera transmission 2012-12-01..2013-05-31. Source states: '7.2 AWD /Dysentery There is no AWD was reported for the last six months in both zones.'. Evidence type: Documented_Absence. Surveillance system status during absence: operational. AGENT 3 (opus55) batch 1 Q11. Zone-level documented absence from the 2013 Belg season health assessment of East and West Hararghe zones, Oromia (data January-May 2013; visited woredas incl. Melkabelo, Meta, Grawa, Medega Tola, Meyu, Chinaksen in East Hararghe and Tullo, Habro/Hawi Gudina, Boke Dimtu, Doba in West Hararghe), reproduced in an Ethiopian FETP thesis. DATING: 'the last six months' before the assessment = Dec 2012-May 2013. SURVEILLANCE WAS LOOKING: the same section reports 335 suspected malaria cases by woreda (Grawa 177), 12 measles cases plus 8 confirmed and 3 measles deaths in Chinaksen, one suspected meningitis case, and monthly OTP admissions (East Hararghe 3,325 SAM Jan-May 2013; West Hararghe 1,050), from zone health department and district health office data. A second thesis (Dagnachew Alemu, prior-cycle Agent 4 note, AAU c8287853) states 'In the last three years (2012-2014 GC), epidemic of AWD was not occurred in both East and West Harerghe Zones' - weaker ('no epidemic'), not used for the window but consistent. REGIONAL CONTEXT: the zones border Somali region (cholera in Somalia every year 2012-2015) and had AWD in Sep-Nov 2011 (Index 715-720, 866-869); within-Ethiopia quiet period. Provincial subset - do not sum with national row.

source: Tessema Tarekegn, Compiled Body of Works in Field Epidemiology, Ethiopian FETP, Addis Ababa University, May 2015 (AAU ETD) - SNNPR Belg season assessment 6-21 June 2014 (EC 2006), Gamo-Gofa (Kamba, Merab-Abaya) and Wolayta (Humbo, Boloso-Sore) zones, data January-May 2014
processing_notes: Source confirms zero cholera transmission 2014-01-01..2014-05-31. Source states: 'Malaria was the top cause for morbidity both in adults and under five children in all woredas for the last five months. Measles outbreak was reported from Merab-Abaya woreda of Gamo-Gofa zone. No AWD, and meningococcal meningitis cases were reported from the four woredas.'. Evidence type: Documented_Absence. Surveillance system status during absence: operational. AGENT 3 (opus55) batch 1 Q12. Woreda documented absence, January-May 2014, from the SNNPR Belg season health assessment (6-21 June 2014; EC '2006') of Kamba and Merab-Abaya (Gamo-Gofa) and Humbo and Boloso-Sore (Wolayta), reproduced in an Ethiopian FETP thesis. SURVEILLANCE WAS LOOKING: the same section tabulates the top morbidity causes by woreda for Jan-May 2014 (e.g. Boloso-Sore 1,260 adult malaria cases, 140 under-5 diarrhoea, 104 dysentery), monthly malaria and SAM rates for all four woredas, and a measles outbreak in Merab-Abaya; coordination described as functional. Abuts (does not overlap) the Jun-Oct 2014 zeros for the same woredas from a separate assessment (Index 1002-1007, source 223), giving documented absence across Jan-Oct 2014. REGIONAL CONTEXT: within-Ethiopia quiet period (national 2014 undetermined; JHU 2014 zero is a phantom). Provincial subset - do not sum with national row.
